idea-plugin.name: Maven Assist
idea-plugin.description:
Your friendly co-pilot for pom.xml files. Maven Assist detects whether the directory you point it at already contains a pom — and gives you exactly the right tools for both cases: create a brand-new pom in seconds, or inspect and update an existing one with one-click version upgrades straight from Maven Central. 🚀

✨ Features at a glance

  • 📂 Works in any directory — pick a folder, the whole workflow runs right there.
  • 🔍 Automatic detection — instantly switches between "create" and "manage" mode.
  • 🆕 Pom creation wizard — parent pom via path, dependencies picked from a searchable list, newest versions pre-selected.
  • ⬆️ One-click updates — every dependency gets an Update button that bumps it to the newest version and builds.
  • ➕ Searchable dependency picker — every list shows just the name plus a Details button per row (coordinates & versions on demand): search, tick, Add — inserted into the pom automatically, build included.
  • 🎯 Per-dependency versions — after picking, a second step lets you choose for each dependency: newest version, a specific version, and auto update.
  • 🔄 Auto update on save — flag dependencies (shown green/red in the table) and they jump to the newest version every time you save the project.
  • 📌 Extensible manager — give it a name, paste any dependency snippet once, keep it in your catalog forever.
  • 🧼 Formatting preserved — edits are surgical; even ${property} versions are handled correctly.
  • 🎨 Visually customizable plugin page — enter edit mode and drag & drop buttons to move them, click any button to change its text, colors and size live, and use checkboxes to pick per field (version, group id, newest version, …) whether it appears directly in the table or only under Details. Saved permanently.

🚀 How to use

1) Open the tool window

Click Maven Assist on the right edge of the IDE (or View → Tool Windows → Maven Assist). The directory field at the top starts at your project root — pick any other folder with the folder button right beside the field (or type a path and press Enter) and the view rescans instantly.

2) No pom.xml yet? Create one 🆕

  • Fill in group id, artifact id and version.
  • Optionally pick a parent pom with Choose Path… — coordinates and relativePath are filled in for you.
  • Tick the dependencies you want in the list — search to filter it; each row shows only the name, and Details reveals coordinates and the newest version.
  • Leave “Always use the newest version” checked (it is by default) and every selected dependency is created with the latest release from Maven Central.
  • Hit Create pom.xml — done. The view switches straight to the dependency table.

3) Pom already there? Manage it 📋

  • See every dependency with its version — including versions resolved from properties.
  • Search the list and filter it with one click: Only newest version (already up to date) and Only auto update (flagged for auto-updating).
  • An Open button next to the pom path (and next to the parent pom, when it resolves to a file) opens the file right in the editor.
  • Check for Updates fills the Newest Version column for all rows, and Update All bumps every dependency in the pom to its newest version at once (one build at the end).
  • Press Update right next to a row's version and choose Newest version or Custom version… (type your own): Maven Assist rewrites the pom and runs mvn compile — you just watch the notification. ⚡
  • The red trash button at the far right of every row deletes the dependency from the pom — after a confirmation, of course. 🗑️ The trash button next to the search bar enters multi-select mode: tick several dependencies and delete them all at once.

4) Add dependencies ➕

Click Add Dependencies — adding is a friendly two-step flow:

  • Step 1 — pick: type in the search bar and tick what you need. Each row shows only the dependency's name; the Details button reveals group id, artifact id, catalog/pinned version and the newest version from Maven Central.
  • Step 2 — configure: press Next and every selected dependency gets its own block with Use newest version, a Specific version field and an Auto update on every project save checkbox — all chosen per dependency (Back returns to the list without losing anything).

Press Add and the dependencies land in your pom exactly as configured; a build kicks off automatically. Auto-updated ones stay on the newest version forever (see below).

5) Auto update on every save 🔄

The dependency table has an auto update column — green means on, red means off, and a click toggles it. Whenever you save the project, Maven Assist checks all green-flagged dependencies against Maven Central and bumps them to the newest version automatically (pom rewritten + build). The tool window also reloads itself on every save, so what you see always matches what is on disk.

6) Grow your own catalog 📌

Click Add Own to Manager… at the bottom of the Add Dependencies window (the create view also has an Add Dependencies to Manager button), give the dependency a name and paste its code — a <dependency>…</dependency> block from mvnrepository.com or a plain groupId:artifactId:version line — then press Add. It is stored permanently under that name and shows up in every picker from now on, in all projects, across IDE restarts. Don't need one anymore? Every picker row also has a red trash button that deletes the dependency from the manager entirely (after a confirmation) — built-in catalog entries included.

7) Make the page yours 🎨

Click the blue Customize… link in the bottom-left corner of the tool window and a separate customize window opens with a live preview of the whole plugin page — top bar, dependency table (with sample data) and the details-dialog buttons:

  • 🖱️ Drag & drop any button — it lifts off and sticks to your mouse as a ghost while an animated gap glides to where it would land. Drop it anywhere: reorder within a section or move it between the top bar and the details dialog. Moved buttons keep working (e.g. Update to Newest Version in the main window acts on the selected row).
  • ↔️ Resize by dragging — grab a button's right edge to pull it wider, the bottom edge to make it taller, or the corner for both, exactly like a window. A resized button keeps its size; untouched ones keep filling the row.
  • 🎨 Click a button in the preview and a small floating editor appears: change its text, background & text color, width, height and font size — every change shows up in the preview instantly, so you always see exactly what you get.
  • ☑️ The Visible fields checkboxes decide for every dependency field (name, group id, artifact id, version, newest version, auto update) whether it is shown directly in the table or under "Details" — preview columns appear/disappear as you tick.
  • 💾 The real plugin window is untouched while you experiment. Press Save and your design is applied to it and kept forever (across restarts); Cancel throws the changes away. Reset All to Defaults returns to the factory layout.

💡 Good to know

  • Builds use your project's mvnw wrapper if present, otherwise mvn from the PATH.
  • Automatic builds after pom changes run mvn compile (fast). Need the full thing? The MVN Clean Install button at the very bottom runs mvn clean install.
  • No Maven installed? The plugin automatically falls back to the Maven bundled with your IDE — so builds usually just work. If even that is missing, MVN Clean Install offers to install Maven for you (Homebrew/winget, or downloaded from apache.org — into the project or for the whole machine, your choice).
  • Version lookups run in the background; the IDE never freezes. 🧊
